title: Fight Club — The life you own

hook.quote: The first rule of Fight Club is: you do not talk about Fight Club.
hook.context: Tyler yashirin klub a'zolariga qoidalarni e'lon qiladi. "do not talk" — qat'iy buyruq ohangi uchun qisqartirilmagan shakl (don't emas). Bu qoida eng mashhur kino iqtiboslaridan biriga aylangan.

reading: The narrator has a good office job and a flat full of expensive furniture. From the outside his life looks successful, but he can't sleep and he feels empty inside.
He often thinks, "If I had a more interesting life, I would be happy." He buys more and more things, but nothing changes.
On a business trip he meets Tyler Durden, a soap salesman who is everything the narrator is not: free, confident and completely careless about rules.
Tyler tells him that people are slaves to the things they own. "If you lost everything tomorrow," he asks, "who would you really be?"
Together they start a secret club where tired office workers come to fight. The men feel alive for the first time in years.
Slowly the club grows into something much more dangerous. Tyler's ideas become a movement, and the narrator realises he has lost control of his own life.
The film asks an uncomfortable question: if we didn't measure ourselves by money and possessions, how would we measure our lives?

grammar.title: Second Conditional: if I had..., I would...
explain: **Second conditional** — hozirgi yoki kelajakdagi **xayoliy, real bo'lmagan** vaziyat: **If** + Past Simple, **would** + fe'l. **If** I **had** a more interesting life, I **would be** happy (hozir unday hayot yo'q).
Shakl o'tmishga o'xshaydi, lekin ma'no hozirgi. "If you lost everything tomorrow" — ertangi kun haqida, faqat ehtimoli kam.
**to be** bilan rasmiy ingliz tilida barcha shaxslar uchun **were**: If I **were** you, I would change jobs. Og'zaki nutqda "if I was" ham uchraydi.
First bilan farqi: If I **win** the lottery, I **will** buy a house (sizningcha real). If I **won** the lottery, I **would** buy a house (deyarli imkonsiz).
